definitions.expert_bpw: bits per logical expert parameter (scales billed separately in source_effective)
definitions.f_expert: logical params of routed_expert + shared_expert weights / all logical params
definitions.logical_params: Unpacked source parameters: I8 FP4-packed weights count as 2 logical elements per stored byte (native_k = 2 * packed_k). F8_E4M3/BF16/F32 weights count prod(shape). UE8M0 scales and I64 tid2eid tables are sidecar bytes, not logical params.
definitions.stored_element_bpw: 8 * bytes / prod(shape) across the organ; this is the 8.08-class figure

bpw_feasibility_envelope.scale_sidecar_note: Source expert_bytes already include UE8M0 scales. The envelope table treats expert_bpw as the complete expert rate a child would bill (weights+scales+codebooks) per logical expert param.

prior_runtime_accounting_check.verdict: The 145 MB vs 103 MB split is a PER-TOKEN SERVED traffic figure, not a stored-parameter split. Stored byte mass is overwhelmingly routed experts. The 102,760,448 MoE number reproduces exactly as 6*routed_fp4_weights + shared_fp8_weights + gate.weight (NO scales). The 144,703,488 attention number reproduces exactly as MLA_fp8_weights + shared_fp8_weights + ONE routed_fp4_expert_weights — that is not a clean attention-only mass. A 1.5 COMPLETE budget still cannot ignore MLA/mHC/indexer/router: they dominate served bytes/token even though they are a small fraction of stored mass.
